h1: Clear Braces & Invisible Aligners in Fort Worth, TX
intro: Straighten your teeth without anyone knowing you're in treatment. Custom-made, virtually invisible aligner trays gently shift your teeth into perfect alignment — no metal brackets, no wires, no dietary restrictions, and no impact on your professional appearance.

sections.h2: What Are Clear Braces & How Do They Work?
body: Clear braces — also called invisible aligners or clear aligners — are a revolutionary alternative to traditional metal orthodontics. Instead of brackets and wires, your teeth are moved using a series of custom-made, crystal-clear plastic trays that fit snugly and comfortably over your teeth.

Each set of trays is worn for approximately 1–2 weeks, applying gentle and precise pressure that gradually shifts your teeth by small increments toward their final aligned positions. You receive a new set of trays at regular intervals throughout your treatment — each one moving your teeth a little closer to perfect alignment.

Because the aligners are removable, you simply take them out to eat, drink, brush, and floss — then put them back in. No dietary restrictions, no special cleaning tools, no emergency wire-poking appointments. Just discreet, predictable tooth movement that fits seamlessly into your life.
bullets: Custom-fitted from precise digital impressions of your teeth
BPA-free medical-grade plastic — safe and comfortable
Changed every 1–2 weeks as teeth progressively shift
Dr. Brown monitors your progress at regular check-ins

sections.h2: 6 Reasons Fort Worth Adults Choose Clear Braces
body: Clear aligners have transformed orthodontic treatment for adults who want straight teeth without the drawbacks of traditional metal braces.
bullets: Virtually invisible — crystal-clear plastic blends seamlessly with your teeth; most people won't know you're in treatment at all
No food restrictions — simply remove your aligners before eating and replace them afterward; no forbidden foods, no broken brackets
Easy oral hygiene — remove your aligners to brush and floss exactly as normal, with no special tools or threading floss under wires
Comfortable treatment — no sharp metal edges or wire adjustments; gentle, consistent pressure with only mild discomfort when changing trays
Predictable results — digital treatment planning lets Dr. Brown show you a projected map of how your teeth will move at each stage
Professional-friendly — straighten your teeth while maintaining a polished, confident appearance at work

body: Clear aligners are effective for correcting a wide range of orthodontic issues in both adults and teenagers. Dr. Brown will assess your teeth and bite during your consultation to confirm whether clear braces are the right treatment for your specific case.
bullets: Crowded teeth — overlapping or closely packed teeth
Gapped teeth — spaces or diastema between teeth
Overbite — upper teeth significantly overlap lower
Underbite — lower teeth protrude in front of upper
Crossbite — upper and lower teeth don't align correctly
Open bite — upper and lower teeth don't touch when biting
Relapsed orthodontics — teeth that have shifted after previous treatment
Minor misalignment — slightly twisted or rotated individual teeth

sections.h2: How Your Clear Braces Treatment Works
body: From your first consultation to your final beautifully straight smile, here's exactly what the process looks like.
bullets: Consultation & scan — Dr. Brown examines your teeth, takes X-rays, and creates precise digital impressions (no messy putty); a digital treatment plan shows the projected movement of your teeth at every stage
Custom trays fabricated — your complete series of custom aligner trays is fabricated from medical-grade BPA-free plastic, each one moving your teeth incrementally toward the final position
Wear & progress — you wear each set of trays for 20–22 hours per day, changing to a new set every 1–2 weeks, with periodic check-ins so Dr. Brown can monitor progress
Retainer & results — when treatment is complete, you'll wear a custom retainer to maintain your results; this is essential, as teeth can gradually shift back without retention

sections.h2: Clear Braces vs. Traditional Metal Braces
body: Understanding the key differences helps you choose the right path to your straight smile. Clear braces are a great fit if you have mild to moderate crowding, spacing, or bite issues, want discreet treatment, and are disciplined about wearing aligners 20–22 hours per day. Other options may be better for severe malocclusion, complex jaw discrepancies, active untreated decay or gum disease, or significant bite correction requiring more force. Dr. Brown will always recommend the most effective treatment for your specific case — never just the most popular option.
bullets: Visibility: virtually invisible vs. clearly visible metal
Removability: fully removable vs. fixed
Food restrictions: none — remove to eat vs. many restrictions
Oral hygiene: normal brushing and flossing vs. special tools required
Treatment duration: 6–18 months for most cases vs. 18–36 months typically
Emergency visits: rarely needed vs. broken wires and brackets common

faqs.q: What are clear braces and how do they work?
faqs.a: Clear braces are a series of custom-made, virtually invisible removable plastic aligner trays that progressively shift your teeth into proper alignment. Each tray in the series is slightly different from the last, applying gentle pressure that moves teeth by small, precise increments. You wear each set of trays for 1–2 weeks, then move on to the next set. Over the course of 6–18 months (depending on case complexity), your teeth gradually reach their final aligned positions. Unlike metal braces, you remove the aligners to eat, drink, brush, and floss.

faqs.q: How long does clear braces treatment take?
faqs.a: Treatment duration typically ranges from 6 to 18 months depending on the complexity of your case: minor corrections (small gaps, mild crowding, relapse) take 6 to 9 months; moderate cases (more pronounced crowding or spacing) take 9 to 12 months; and more complex cases (bite correction alongside alignment) take 12 to 18 months. At your consultation, Dr. Brown will use digital treatment planning to provide a realistic projected timeline for your specific case. The most important factor in staying on schedule is wearing your aligners consistently for 20–22 hours per day.

faqs.q: Are clear braces as effective as traditional metal braces?
faqs.a: For mild to moderate alignment issues — crowding, spacing, overbite, underbite, and relapsed orthodontics — clear aligners are just as effective as traditional metal braces, and in many cases achieve results faster. For very severe malocclusion or significant jaw discrepancies, traditional braces or a combined orthodontic/surgical approach may deliver more predictable results. Dr. Brown will give you an honest assessment of whether clear aligners are the optimal treatment for your specific situation at your consultation.

faqs.q: Can I eat and drink with clear braces in?
faqs.a: You should always remove your aligners before eating or drinking anything other than plain water. Eating with aligners in can crack the trays and trap food particles against your teeth, and hot drinks can warp the plastic. The great news is this means absolutely no food restrictions during treatment. Enjoy whatever you like — just remove, eat, rinse your mouth, and reinsert your aligners. A small, discreet aligner case (provided with your treatment) is perfect for storing them safely during meals.

Most patients experience mild pressure and slight soreness for the first day or two after switching to a new set of trays — this is completely normal and is a sign that the aligners are working. This discomfort is generally mild and resolves quickly. Clear aligners are generally considered significantly more comfortable than traditional metal braces, which can cause irritation to the cheeks and lips from brackets and wires. There are no sharp edges, no emergency wire poking, and no bracket-related sores with clear aligners.

faqs.q: Will clear braces affect my speech?
faqs.a: Most patients experience a very brief adjustment period of a few days where speech may feel slightly different — particularly with certain sounds like "s" or "th". This is completely normal and resolves quickly as your tongue and mouth adapt to the presence of the aligners. The vast majority of patients find that clear aligners have minimal long-term impact on their speech — certainly far less than the brackets and wires of traditional metal braces.

faqs.q: Is clear braces treatment covered by dental insurance?
faqs.a: Some dental insurance plans include orthodontic benefits that may cover a portion of clear braces treatment — typically a fixed lifetime orthodontic benefit amount. Coverage varies significantly by plan and by whether you have exhausted any prior orthodontic benefit. Our team will verify your specific orthodontic benefits before treatment begins and provide a full written cost estimate. We offer flexible financing options with low and 0% interest options to make treatment accessible for every budget.

faqs.q: Will I need to wear a retainer after treatment?
faqs.a: Yes — retainer wear after treatment is essential and non-negotiable. Teeth have a natural tendency to drift back toward their original positions after orthodontic treatment, known as relapse. A retainer holds your teeth in their new aligned positions while the surrounding bone and tissue permanently stabilize. Dr. Brown provides custom retainers at the end of your treatment. Options include removable clear retainers (worn nightly) or fixed bonded retainers (thin wires bonded behind your front teeth). In many cases a combination of both provides the best long-term protection.
